Notes to Authors

It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity.

The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyas), consensus (Ijma'), and personal thought (Ijtihad). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference. Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint.

Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations. This is to avoid the inadvertent mental re-translation to an Arabic composition which is different from the original.

Every Hadith should be accompanied by its sources (transmitters) and the reference book where it may be found. If the transmitter(s) and/or the reference book were not known, this should be stated clearly.

ERRATUM
God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

In the last issue of ISLAM [1(2): 91-104], it was pointed out that the only 2 suras in the Qur'an which are initialed with the letter Qaf [namely, sura Al-Shura (No. 42) and sura Qaf (No. 50)] contain exactly the same number of this letter, i.e. 57; that the total number of occurrences of this letter in the 2 suras is 114, the same as the total number of suras in the Qur'an. It was pointed out that this deliberate design and the knowledge of the mathematical distribution of individual alphabets throughout the Qur'an are unattainable by man; that only Allah could have such capability. Allah (the most glorified, most high) placed the initial Qaf at the beginning of the 2 suras to indicate to us His knowledge of the alphabetical distribution; that there is something special about the letter Qaf in these particular suras; that only He is the author of the Qur'an.

On page 98 of that article, however, it was pointed out that sura Ibrahim (No. 14) is the only other sura where the letter Qaf occurs 57 times. I am writing this erratum to state that, in comparing the number of occurrences of the letter Qaf, I have overlooked the fact that while suras Al-Shura & Qaf have the letter Qaf prefixed to them, sura Ibrahim is not initialed with the letter Qaf. If the letter Qaf is prefixed as an initial in sura Ibrahim, for a fair and accurate comparison, then the number of occurrences of the letter Qaf will become 58, not the same as the 2 Qaf-initialed suras. To look at it another way, if we remove all the Qur'anic initials from the Qur'an, we will find that sura Qaf and sura Al-Shura contain 56 Qafs each, while sura Ibrahim contains 57 Qafs. It was neither fair, nor accurate, therefor, to state that sura Ibrahim was "the only other sura which contains the same number of Qafs as the Qaf-initialed suras."

We can easily envision that Allah (the most glorified, most high) looked at His complete message to humanity, the Qur'an, before the placement of the Qur'anic initials and knew that only two suras qualify to receive the initial Qaf so that the total number of Qafs in them would equal the total number of suras. These two suras were Al-Shura (No. 42) and Qaf (No. 50). In order to give us a signal or a hint that He alone knows the alphabetical [text continues on next page]

THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS"

According to Church historians, the Gospel of Barnabas does not exist as a complete manuscript, but survives only in fragments and certain ecclesiastical writings of the first and second centuries of the Chrisitian Era. It was written in Greek. It is extremely difficult to find a copy of what exists, either in Greek or in translation. But there does exist another book, a complete manuscript, which calls itself the "Gospel of Barnabas". Allegedly it was written in Hebrew when it was discovered by Pope Sixtus V (1585-1590 CE), who is said to have translated it from Hebrew into Italian. This Italian "Barnabas" later found its way into the Hofbiblyothek at Vienna, and was translated into English in 1907 by Lonsdale and Laura Ragg. Strangely, the Italian edition has Arabic footnotes.3

The Italian "Barnabas" could not have been written by a disciple of Jesus Christ in the first century C.E. This is the judgment of Christian scholars who have read "Barnabas" and it is one in which this Muslim reader will have to concur. To be sure, it mentions the blessed prophet Muhammad by name, but this presents the first problem. "Barnabas" mentions Muhammad by name much too often for a Christian Gospel. In fact, "Barnabas" mentions Muhammad by name more often than the Qur'an does. At the same time, it contains doctrines which are not approved by either orthodox Christian or Muslim tradition. A chief example of this is the assertion by "Barnabas" that Jesus is not the Messiah and that Jesus cursed Peter for calling him the Messiah.4 By contrast, the Qur'an makes several references to Al-Masih, 'Isa b. Maryam, "The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary." There is no disagreement between Islam and Christianity on this point.

For a book supposedly written in Hebrew originally, "Barnabas" uses defective Hebrew in transliteration. Jesus reportedly raises his "eyes to heaven (saying): 'O Elohim Sabaoth, have mercy upon thy servants.'" (p. 21) This construction "Elohim Sabaoth" (God of Hosts) is Greek, not Hebrew. The correct Hebrew form would be Elohei Sabaoth or Elohei has-sabaoth.5 On page 34, "Barnabas" records that "Jesus went to Jerusalem, near unto the Senofegia, a feast of our nation." If this were originally a Hebrew book, the correct term would be Sukkoth, not Senofegia. The reference is to the Feast of Tabernacles, which is Hag has-sukkoth in the Hebrew Bible (Deuteronomy 16:13; Zachariah 14:16, etc.), and skenopegia in New Testament Greek (John 7:2). The reading in "Barnabas", Senofegia, is a Latin form, which points up something very disturbing about this book.

Much of Barnabas shows a dependence on the Latin Bible, rather than either the Hebrew Scriptures or the Greek New Testament. For example, in quoting Psalm 50, "Barnabas" writes verses 13 and 14 first and then joins part of verse 12 at the end, making the sense different from that of the [continues]

The dependence on the Vulgate proves that "Barnabas" could have been written not earlier than 350 years after the mission of Jesus!

"Barnabas" quotes from the Old Testament apocryphal book called Susanna (p. 60) which was in the Vulgate, but not in the Hebrew canon. And if the book were written by the Barnabas of the first century, it would never have carried the serious blunder found on page 76 of the English edition. Here "Barnabas" says: "The passover drew near, wherefore Jesus, which his disciples, went up to Jerusalem. And he went to the pool called 'Probatica'." "Probatica" was not the name of the pool! The name of the pool was Bethesda ("House of Mercy" in Hebrew) or Bethzatha ("House of the Olive"), according to some manuscripts. The name of the pool seems to have been connected with the miracles which were said to have taken place there, as "Barnabas" admits: "And the bath (pool) was so called because the angel of God every day troubled the water, and whosoever first entered the water after its movement was cured of every kind of infirmity." (p. 76, cf. John 5:2-4. However, this explanation of the name Bethesda is not included in the earliest manuscripts of the New Testament and some modern translations omit it. It is thus the more curious that "Barnabas" includes a portion of the New Testament which is based on later manuscripts and then misinterprets its meaning!) "Probatica", which "Barnabas" mistakes for the name of the pool, is really the name for the sheep-gate which was near the pool. "Probatica" is the Latin form of the Greek New Testament word probatika at John 5:2, meaning "Sheep Gate". How could a book written originally in Hebrew overlook the very Hebrew name of the miraculous pool, Bethesda, and put in its place a word of Greek derivation which referred, not to the pool at all, but to its gate?

The Italian "Barnabas" is full of fables. Unlike the Qur'an, which insists upon making no distinctions between the prophets, "Barnabas" protrays Muhammad (peace be upon him) in an almost Divine light, setting him over and above all the rest to a fabulous degree. The passage which Muslims like to quote wherein Jesus foretells the coming of Muhammad, having denied the Messiahship to Jesus, gives it to the Prophet: "Jesus answered: 'The name of the Messiah is Admirable (Muhammad).'" (p. 113) But Muhammad (peace be upon him) never claimed to be the Messiah, nor does the Qur'an say that Jesus foretold the coming of a Messiah, but of another rasul. Therefore, even this oft-used verse of "Barnabas" has a fatal flaw.

"Barnabas" could not have been written before the fourth century C.E. and there is evidence that it was written even much later, somewhere in Medieval

Here "Barnabas" again denies the messiahship to Jesus and gives it to Muhammad, but he also speaks of the Jubilee "which now cometh every hundred years . . ." at the time of the disciple Barnabas, the Jubilee came every fifty years! The Jubilee which "now cometh every hundred years" could only refer to the Papal Jubilee of the Catholic Church, which was inaugurated in 1300 C.E. and reduced to 50 years in 1350 C.E. Furthermore, many of the doctrines contained in this 'gospel' are clearly contradictory to the teachings of Islam."8 The disciple Barnabas of the Bible was not even an eyewitness to the mission of Jesus, though this claim is made in the Italian "Barnabas", where his name is placed in the list of the 12 disciples. None of the Gospels of the Bible has Barnabas in the list, nor do they even mention him. We first meet Barnabas in the Book of Acts (4:34), where he is a helper in Paul's missionary work, "a good man full of the holy spirit and faith." If Barnabas has written a Gospel, it would be similarly an honest and faithful narrative of the life of Jesus, worthy of at least as much honor by Christians as the letters of Paul in the Bible, since Paul was not an eyewitness to the ministry of jesus either. But this myth-filled Italian manuscript is not the Gospel of Barnabas. Muslims must look for the real one.

They decided that Israeli withdrawal from Jerusalem should be a paramount and unchangeable prerequisite for lasting peace in the Middle East.

In the early days of Islam, it served as the first Qibla of the Muslims, for they used to pray towards Jerusalem when Muhammad still lived in Mecca. After the Prophet migrated to Medina, he continued to pray towards Jerusalem for 16 months, until he was directed to face towards Mecca.1,2

The Dome of the Rock stands on one of the most sacred spots in the world. It was built by Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik Ibn Marwan in 961 A.D. on the same site where Caliph 'Umar built his mosque of wood. The monument is of such noble beauty that it stands unrivalled in the real of sacred art. It is one of the two oldest and most impressive specimens of the early Muslim architecture, the other being the Grand Mosque of Damscuss which has remained intact to this day. The temple area or the Haram al-Shar-if, as it is called by the Arabs, has always been a place of great sanctity for the Muslims all over the world.

Jerusalem was captured by the Crusaders under Godfrey of Bouillon in July, 1099 A.D. who converted the mosque into a church and renamed it Templum Dominini. They even built an altar on the Rock. But Sultan Salahuddin, in October, 1187 A.D., recaptured it.3,4,5

After the death of the Sultan, Jerusalem remained under Muslim rule for 731 years. It was ruled in turn by the Ayubites, Mamlukes and finally the Ottomans until 1918, when it was captured by the British forces led by General Allenby.

Even in 1917, General Allenby, upon entering the Old City of Jerusalem and being told that the Keys of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre had been kept for centuries by the Muslims for the daily opening and locking of the Church, observed that he could not be more than the Caliph 'Umar, and therefor the keys should continue to be in the hands of the Arab Muslims.

Mu'ammar Al-Qadhafi, Chief of State, Libyan Arab Republic

Islam & World Governments: The Third International Theory

IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE MOST COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL

In a world where tensions and conflicts abound and in which materialism, whether capitalist or communist, is blinding human beings from the spiritual values of life, a comeback to religion is now gaining momentum.

Life on earth, being as it is, a preparation for the hereafter has stopped to be so in the absence of a genuine religious drive. Man, all through the world, is now working as if he were to exist on earth forever. He has ostensibly set aside spiritual values, the result of which is that he is drifting away in a whirlpool of materialistic values. God, apparently, is being deliberately or unconsciously forgotten . . .

State policies, in their turn, are simply inspired nowadays by mundane and materialistic objectives. Social and economic interrelations among humans are subsequently suffering. Man, today, is groping his way towards complete loss sacrificing his age-old spiritual security and happiness for some few moments of satisfaction he succeeds to snatch every now and then.

In olden times when religion was supreme, there were no man-made theories. Only religion — the divine theory — predominated, and in its shade, man knew happiness and security for he duly felt he was the successor of God on earth. However, human self-conceit and other factors have put the veils on our eyes. Serfdom at one time, was institutionalized and gained sway.

Physical force was instrumental to subdue the freeborn individual and, when conflict of interests increased among the masters, they agreed to replace serfdom with the feudal system. Riches on the earth became the instruments of power as the feudal lords possessed not only the land but also the lives of men working within the confines of this property. In the meantime inter-human exploitation spread in the cities, at first, in a limited way, during the pre-industrial Revolution Age, and, then world-wide after James Watt's discovery of steam.

The Church, too, had its part in exploiting Man, and flagrantly digressing from true Christianity in the era of the Borgias, began to sell indulgence bonds for the remission of temporal and especially purgatorial punishment.

THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

Clergymen, in the Age of Decadence, were notorious feudal lords, who committed abuses of power as well as other forms of exploitation. Protestantism, a movement which caused a schism within the church, failed to reform the clergy who kept digressing from true Christianity. The Inquisition era is also a saliant –digression from Christian tolerance.

Islam, Judaism and even the other non-heavenly creeds have also passed through their own setbacks. But, Islam, for one, has suffered no distortions in its Holy Book though there is a general consensus that some Muslims have had their abuses which caused gross injury to Muslims at large. However, Judaism had been flagrantly distored to suit the purposes of Zionism. The distortions, it is noted, occurred in the Bible and in the Gospels while, in Islam, only the misbehaviour of some Muslims is detected. (see this issue).

Screening back the evolution of history, it is found that theoricians like David Ricardo and Adam Smith, began to interpret life in terms of capitalist thinking. Of course, Man tried to revolt against exploitation. Theoretically, humanitarian thinkers, philosophers and economists, like St. Simon, Owen, Lasalle and Proudhon appeared and, tried, in their own way, to establish a utopian society of their own. Practically, however, a true mass revolution took place in the year 1789 in France, calling for Liberty, Fraternity and Equality, but this outburst was short-lived as France reverted to militarism to spread its empire.

The communist theory emerged in the year 1848 in a manifesto entirely based on dialectical materialism, which maintains that the basis of reality is constantly changing in a dialectical process giving the priority of matter over mind and metaphysics. This ideology was aimed, in fact, to be against inter-human exploitation but it appeared to be a theory that disregards spiritual values and leaves Man erring astray.

Be all that as it is, the First of September Revolution in the Libyan Arab Republic feels it is its duty to remind Mankind of the necessity for a comeback to God. For humanity, as a whole, is now in dire need for a new path which is to take us back to our religions and to God who created us to be His successors on earth.

The "Third International Theory" is not a new theory but has been purposely called so for it, partly, screens out the drawbacks of the other two theories now in practice in the world, namely, capitalism and communism, and, partly, because it urges Mankind for a return to God by adopting a third path, different from the two existing ones.
